baroreceptor stimulation activates the locus ceruleous and this nucleus innervates the DBB, and that the DBB may be important in the inhibition of vasopression-releasing neurons in response to baroreceptor activation.
noradrenerigic neurons in the locus ceruleous participate in the baroceptor activation of the DB and may be important in the regulation of supraoptic nucleus vasopressin releasing neurons.
baroreceptor activation inhibits vasopressin release from the supraoptic nucleus and this effect is dependent on noradrenergics from the locus coeruleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the locus coeruleus (LC) in baroreceptor activation of the supraoptic vasopression neurons.
the role of the locus cerulens in baroreceptor control of supraoptic vaspressin neurons.
the role of the locus cerulues in baroreceptor activation of the diagonal band and inhibition of vasopresin neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LC is the source of barosensitive noradrenergergic input to the DBB.
the locus ceruleous is a major source of the noradrenergics innervation to the diagonal band of broca.
the locus coeruleus is the primary source of baroreflex-induced noradrenergically-mediated inhibition of supraoptic vasomotor neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LC plays an important role in baroreceptor inhibition of vasopressive neurons.

the LC is the major source of baroreflex-related noradrenergeic innervation to the DBB and that the baroreflex-induced activation of LC neurons may be important in the inhibition of vasopression release from the supraoptic nucleus in the rat.

baroreceptor activation increases Fos expression in noradrenergically innervated neurons in the LC and that this LC activation is required for the baroreflex-induced inhibition of supraoptic vasodilatory neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
baroreceptor activation of supraoptic neurons is not a direct effect of the baroreceptors, but is a complex process involving multiple brainstem regions.
the noradrenergically innervated DBB plays a key role in the baroreceptor inhibition of vasopressing neurons in the supraotic nucleus.
the locus ceruleous (LC), a region of the brain that is important for attention and arousal, is also involved in baroreflex inhibition.
